audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Cho'Gath levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items and made level 6 'Skill', while whys[1], whys[2] and whys[6] on the same page say Maokai owns 2, 3 and the two-item window, and whys[4] calls level 6 Cho'Gath's spike.
audit.why: The packet chart and the already-published mirror audit both read Skill / Maokai / Maokai / Skill / Cho'Gath / Skill / Maokai. The page contradicted its own why text on five of seven rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 1,2,4,5,6 flipped in both layers to match the mirror exactly, ratings adjusted from Maokai's side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rupture — the page's focus ability — carried no cooldown, and neither did Feral Scream or Feast.
audit.why: Rupture is a flat 6s, so 'engage when it is down' is a very short window; Feral Scream is 11s at rank 1 and is the ability that actually costs you the combo; Feast is 80s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d now carry all of them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feast was treated as unavoidable ('if he lands the full lockdown I'm not surviving it') and Twisted Advance's untargetability was never mentioned.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is untargetable for the whole dash, so a Feast cast into it finds no target. The real danger is Feral Scream's silence landing before you cast, not during.
audit.corrected: report[5].t and mid now state the untargetable dash and put the silence in the right place in the sequence.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late were written in first person.
audit.why: Voice break against the rest of the site.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in second person at length.

edits.before: - Cho'Gath Rupture: matchup-defining — Telegraphed. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rupture: a flat 6s and telegraphed — sidestep it, it is his only pre-6 poke. - Feral Scream: 11s silence, the one that costs you the Q follow-up. - Feast: 80s true damage. - Nature's Grasp: 130s.

edits.before: Telegraphed. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: A flat 6s and telegraphed — sidestep it and step up in the gap.

edits.before: Track Cho'Gath's Rupture (Knockup): Telegraphed. Dodge it. When it is down — W-Q + R him.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is untargetable in flight — a Feast cast into the dash finds nothing.

edits.before: Cho'Gath is just as weak at level 1 as I am, but I spike first: once I complete W (Twisted Advance) into Q (Bramble Smash) at 2-3 I can root him onto the spot, poke, and heal the whole trade back with Sap Magic before he has any answer. He has no Feast stacks yet, so my magic damage actually means something here — punish every minion he steps up for. The one thing to dodge is his Rupture (Q) knockup; it's his only real poke pre-6, so don't stand on top of a sapling-cleared wave where he can land it blind.
edits.after: Cho'Gath is just as weak at level 1 as you are, but you spike first: once W (Twisted Advance) into Q (Bramble Smash) are online at 2-3 you root him on the spot, poke, and heal the whole trade back with Sap Magic before he has an answer. He has no Feast stacks yet, so your magic damage still means something — punish every minion he steps up for. The one thing to dodge is Rupture; it is a flat 6s and his only real poke pre-6, so don't stand still where he can land it blind.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still a window where my root cooldowns and Sap Magic let me repeat favourable trades, but I have to start respecting his stacks. Level 6 is where it flips hard: his Rupture knockup into Feral Scream silence chains me long enough for a Feast (R) chomp, and that R is percent-HP true damage that blows straight through my resists and out-paces my heal. Don't W into him when his combo is up — bait the Feral Scream silence and the Rupture first, then trade. If he lands the full lockdown on me, I'm not surviving it even as a tank.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 still let your root cadence and Sap Magic repeat favourable trades, but start respecting his stacks. Level 6 flips it: Rupture knockup into an 11s Feral Scream silence chains you long enough for a Feast chomp, and that R is true damage your resists do nothing about. The order matters — the silence hurts before you cast, not after, since Twisted Advance is untargetable once launched. Bait Feral Scream and Rupture first, then commit; never W in with both up.

edits.before: This is a scaling loss on paper — 44% — because his Feast (R) execute is true damage that ignores everything I build, and he just out-tanks me as a fellow tank with a real damage win condition I don't have. But the 2+ items window is genuinely my one slice of the game: my W-Q lockdown, R (Nature's Grasp) engage wall, and durability still let me catch him and start a fight on my terms, as long as I commit when his Feast is on cooldown. Don't try to grind him down 1v1 in the sidelane — my value is rooting him and his carries in teamfights with Nature's Grasp while my team does the damage I can't.
edits.after: This reads as a scaling loss on paper — 44% — because Feast is true damage that ignores everything you build, and he out-tanks you with a real damage win condition you don't have. But the 2+ items window is genuinely your slice of the game: W-Q lockdown, the Nature's Grasp wall and raw durability still let you catch him and start the fight on your terms, as long as you commit inside his 80s Feast cooldown. Don't grind him down 1v1 in the sidelane — your value is rooting him and his carries in teamfights while your team does the damage you can't.

notes: Chart flipped to match the already-published Cho'Gath-side audit exactly, so mirror-fix.js has nothing to correct. Feral Scream's silence duration is not in the kit data (Riot says only 'a few seconds'), so no number was invented for it — same call the mirror made.
